correctness.rationale: For fully reset position and orientation of planar active Brownian particle with k,γ,v>0, D≥0, independent IID interreset T>0 and E T=m, first moments solve the linear moment ODE giving F(t)=v(e^(−γt)−e^(−kt))/(k−γ), resonance F(t)=vt e^(−kt); G(t)=∫₀ᵗF. Renewal reward gives M(T)=E G(T)/m with finite absolute reward. F has one maximum t₀; H(t)=tF(t)−G(t) has derivative tF′(t) and a unique later positive zero τ. C(t)=F(τ)t for t≤τ and G(t) for t≥τ is the least relevant concave upper envelope. Jensen yields exact supremum F(τ) when m≤τ, and G(m)/m when m≥τ, with equality only deterministic T=m for m≥τ and nonattainment for m<τ; two-point epsilon/τ laws approach bound as epsilon→0. The Poisson rate optimum is r=√(kγ), M=v/(√k+√γ)^2, strictly below best renewal. At k=γ, τk≈1.7932821329 and F≈0.2984256075 v/k vs 0.25 v/k. This is a physical-time signed displacement theorem, not a phase-resolved stationary mean.
residual_risks: The theorem assumes instantaneous full resets with no cost; small-mean burst-clock supremum ceases to be reachable under positive reset overhead.
Any assertion of a unique maximizing strictly positive T law at m<τ would be false; the source carefully states nonattainment.
